items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: That band had Lee Konitz and Zoot Sims and Bill Holman and people like that... But that was the first really American jazz orchestra that I ever encountered.

ctx.x: Did you get a chance to hear any of these artists? Did they ever come to Scotland?

No. Not while I was there. Much later they did. I mean they do now, they travel around quite a bit now. And the thing, I spoke to Conte Candoli last night about this because there was a union ban. The British musicians union didn’t allow American musicians to come in to the country to play. So when Conte Candoli came to Ireland with Stan Kenton in 1953, I was working with an English band that also was working in Dublin at the same time. So we got to see the concert. And that band had Lee Konitz and Zoot Sims and…
At what point in your early years as a saxophonist did you make a conscious decision that you were going to make a living as a musician?
